India's gold imports more than doubled in July, hitting $4.16 billion as buyers treated June's price correction as a chance to own the metal, not trade it.

The World Gold Council puts July volumes at 40 to 45 tonnes against 20 in June, restocking ahead of the festival season. But gold ETF inflows fell 55% in the same month — the jewellery counter came back hard while the investment side pulled back.

The benchmark is already up 9% since that window closed. The festival season will be bought at a price this report doesn't cover.

Gold broke $4,550 an ounce in Beijing on Friday — and ten hours later, New York's close was $48 higher still.

Eastmoney timestamped spot gold at $4,554.44 at 14:51 Beijing time. This paper's mark of record for the same session, Friday's last New York print, is $4,602.40, up $20.80 on the day. Silver fell 0.65% to $68.86, widening the gold-to-silver ratio to 66.84.

China's retail counter is already passing the move through: gold jewellery at one major chain is up 80 yuan a gram in thirteen days. Platinum and palladium stay held today — Kitco and TradingEconomics sit more than a point apart, and a mark no second page confirms doesn't print here.
